competencies.title: Project knowledge for decisions
competencies.meaning: Make established project facts and decisions available in maintained guidance, and connect them to choices made during work. Preserve the information a new executor needs, especially facts that code alone cannot settle; do not reward an exhaustive description of the repository.
competencies.evidence: Trace a task's information need to an authoritative project guide, linked decision, or equivalent accessible source, then to the AI's retrieval and resulting choice. Compare the source with the implementation and confirmed decisions. Look for the project's users, relevant implementation location, domain meaning, or a non-obvious constraint only where it matters to this task. Distinguish an absent fact from an AI ignoring a fact it already read, and attribute each action to its actual actor.
competencies.high: The maintained context supplies the consequential project knowledge, the executor retrieves it through the normal work path, and the resulting work demonstrably uses it without the person reconstructing that knowledge. Appropriate delegated investigation counts. Fictional example: Alder's guide explains that calendar dates belong to the clinic's timezone and points to the clinic profile; AI reads it and builds the calendar using that profile rather than the computer's timezone.
competencies.medium: Useful project knowledge reaches the task, but an established decision is conveyed only through an additional task-time explanation or an incomplete guide requires a consequential correction before the work can use it. Fictional example: Alder's guide identifies clinic staff and the scheduling module, but the person must supply the already agreed clinic-timezone decision after AI proposes the computer's timezone; AI then applies the correction.
competencies.low: The records establish a necessary project fact, show that the active context omits or misstates it, and show work continuing on the wrong basis without an effective correction. Fictional example: an active guide identifies a retired scheduler as authoritative, AI changes it, and inspection confirms the live calendar still uses another implementation. An undiscovered document, a short request, or a file tree alone does not establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: Project knowledge narrows the plausible interpretations of a request. In the fictional calendar change, the timezone decision tells AI whose date the interface must preserve, while the location reference connects that decision to the implementation that can enforce it. This reduces reliance on a fresh explanation of the same project meaning.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when a task depends on project meaning or established decisions beyond its immediate request. Unknown when the needed source, its retrieval, or the resulting choice cannot be observed. Not applicable when no such project-specific knowledge is needed. Do not require the person to document routine facts that the AI can reliably investigate, or penalize an effective delegated investigation.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.note: The repository-knowledge section describes making decisions and reference material discoverable to agents. Adopt discoverability and an inspectable source of truth; its particular repository layout and reported productivity are not scoring requirements or evidence about this person.

competencies.title: Usable operating instructions
competencies.meaning: Maintain actionable directions for the project operations the task actually needs, including working location, prerequisites, environment, relevant commands, and meaningful success conditions. Judge whether the directions enable the workflow, rather than counting commands or demanding every possible procedure.
competencies.evidence: Connect the active directions to actual working directories, dependency or service preparation, selected environment, invoked commands, returned results, and produced artifact. Read the relevant scripts and configuration to check accuracy. Identify whether a failed operation follows an incorrect guide or instead comes from an unrelated environment or implementation defect. A written rule is guidance; enforcement of a prohibited action is separate security evidence.
competencies.high: The executor uses the maintained directions to complete the required project operation in the intended environment, and observed results confirm the directions are usable. Fictional example: Juniper's preview guide identifies the package directory, local service prerequisite, preview command, check command, and artifact destination; AI follows them and obtains the expected preview artifact and actual check result without the person rebuilding the procedure.
competencies.medium: The directions support a substantial part of the operation, but an observed omission or ambiguity requires the person to supply a procedural detail before it succeeds. Fictional example: Juniper's guide provides the browser-check command but omits the local service prerequisite; a connection failure leads the person to provide the startup step, after which the check runs. A failed test that correctly exposes a product defect does not lower this competency.
competencies.low: An established required operation has misleading or demonstrably unpreserved directions, and the resulting execution uses the wrong environment or procedure, or repeatedly reconstructs the same known setup without preserving the correction. Fictional example: a preview-only task follows a guide's production destination and creates an artifact for that destination; the mismatch remains unresolved. Missing run records alone are Unknown, not Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: An operation depends on conditions as well as syntax. Specifying the service prerequisite lets the fictional browser check reach the application; specifying the package directory and destination lets the build act on the intended product variant. Results reveal whether those directions describe a workable procedure.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when the task requires a project-specific setup, check, build, delivery, or comparable operation. Unknown when only written commands are visible and their usability cannot be established. Not applicable when no relevant operation occurs. Existing scripts and delegated execution count; the person need not type commands or restate instructions already applied.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
sources.note: The project-instruction and effective-instruction sections recommend project workflows and concrete, verifiable commands. This supports actionable operating guidance; the documentation also distinguishes contextual instructions from enforced configuration. It does not prove a command ran or that a project's procedure works.

competencies.title: Guidance delivery and reading structure
competencies.meaning: Give each AI executor a working route from shared entry guidance to the specialized information its task needs. Keep active guidance compatible across the tools actually used, and organize detail by a useful scope or task trigger. File length, file count, and automatic injection are not the assessed practice.
competencies.evidence: Follow the effective reading path for the observed client: launch directory, supported discovery settings and overrides, scope rules, explicit reads, references, and retrieved contents. Follow a relevant route into an action that uses the detail. When multiple clients participate, compare the instructions they actually receive. Inspect access or link failures and any repair before judging their effect; do not assume a nested file automatically loads in every client.
competencies.high: The active entry path reaches compatible shared rules and the needed specialized detail, and observed work applies that detail. The structure makes the relevant information available without making unrelated procedures a prerequisite to ordinary work. Fictional example: a Marigold package task follows the entry guide's release route and uses its signing requirement; a separate screen task follows the screen-module route and applies its accessibility rule. A single small guide can also satisfy High when it supplies the relevant context effectively.
competencies.medium: The reading structure delivers useful guidance, but an observed delivery conflict or missing route requires the person's intervention to reach the correct source. Fictional example: one Marigold coding client reads the current startup guide while another receives a stale copy; the second begins with the retired command, then follows the current guide after the person points it out.
competencies.low: A relevant reading-path failure or conflicting delivery is observed, the executor continues without resolving it, and required guidance does not reach the work. Fictional example: Marigold's release link cannot be opened, AI continues without the signing procedure, and the resulting package lacks the required signature. A broken link that is repaired before the guidance is needed does not establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: Information can constrain a decision only after the executor receives it. A useful entry map supplies the next document at the point where its details matter, while a shared authoritative rule avoids competing copies. On-demand retrieval can reduce irrelevant context, but adds navigation work; observed task use determines whether the chosen structure is effective.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an executor must receive maintained project guidance. Evaluate only tools and relevant paths used in the work; multiple tools or multiple files are optional. Unknown when loading or retrieval is unobserved, or when receipt is shown but use is not. Not applicable when no maintained guidance is relevant. Do not impose modular files on an already usable small guide or reward splitting content into imports that all load together.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.note: The context-retrieval section describes lightweight references, retrieval when needed, and a hybrid of initial context and exploration. It also names navigation overhead. Adopt useful progressive disclosure, not a universal rule to minimize file length or retrieve everything lazily.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
sources.note: The discovery section specifies Codex's startup chain from project root to working directory, overrides, fallback names, and a combined size limit. This supports inspecting the effective client path rather than assuming every nested instruction file was injected.

sources.note: The loading, imports, and scoped-rule sections distinguish startup imports from conditional retrieval; AGENTS.md support also depends on client settings and version. Adopt client-aware delivery checks. Neither a shared filename nor an import alone proves relevant guidance influenced work.

competencies.title: Guidance upkeep
competencies.meaning: Keep active project guidance accurate as commands, locations, constraints, and decisions change. Use an applied maintenance mechanism that handles relevant updates as part of work, rather than depending on a new reminder for every correction. Retire superseded directions and preserve valid guidance; do not generate documentation work without a real need.
competencies.evidence: Trace an actual project change or discovered guidance defect to the maintenance trigger, actor, saved authoritative revision, affected references, and check against the new project state. Inspect whether an established rule, workflow step, or automated check caused the update without a task-specific reminder, and whether the repaired route or instruction was usable in actual work. Distinguish a completed update from a promise, and record later reuse only when observed.
competencies.high: An established workflow or automated check triggers the relevant upkeep without a fresh reminder. AI corrects the authoritative guidance and affected routes, removes or clearly retires contradictory active directions, and checks the repaired content against actual project behavior. Fictional example: moving Cedar's exporter triggers the standing module-change rule; AI updates the package route and build directions, removes the retired command, then follows the revised directions to build the new package successfully. A standing instruction counts only when its upkeep behavior actually occurs; a separate scheduler or hook is optional.
competencies.medium: A useful, accurate repair is completed and checked, but the observed process depends on a separate reminder for that maintenance opportunity, or a partial repair demonstrably leaves competing guidance that requires intervention. Fictional example: after Cedar's package move, the person separately requests the documentation repair; AI then corrects the authoritative route, retires the old command, and confirms the new command works. This is effective upkeep with a person still initiating that recurring step.
competencies.low: A concrete change or exposed defect makes an active instruction wrong, a maintenance opportunity is observed, and the wrong direction remains prescribed or is reintroduced without correction. Fictional example: Cedar's exporter move is complete and the obsolete command has been identified, but the active guide still sends the next export task to the removed package. A timestamp, an old document unrelated to the task, or lack of a later session does not establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: An accurate entry guide becomes misleading when its target moves or its procedure changes. Connecting upkeep to the relevant change closes that gap before the next executor relies on it. Retiring the old direction removes an avoidable choice between apparently valid procedures, while a real use of the revised instruction checks more than its wording.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an observed change or demonstrated defect creates a genuine guidance-maintenance need. Not applicable when no relevant upkeep opportunity occurs. Unknown when the update, trigger, or check is not observable; do not downgrade solely because later reuse is unavailable. Human approval of an unsettled policy decision is appropriate and does not prevent High. The AI can maintain confirmed facts automatically without inventing new policy.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.note: The repository-knowledge section describes documentation checks and a recurring agent that compares guidance with code behavior and proposes repairs. This supports applied automatic upkeep; it is one team's engineering account, not proof that a scheduled agent or any exact repository structure is necessary.

sources.title: Encode Lessons in Structure
sources.note: The skill recommends encoding recurring corrections in executable structure where possible, while retaining clearer instructions and failure examples for judgment calls. Adopt the distinction between repeatable mechanical upkeep and human policy judgment; do not turn every documentation edit into a new automation system.

boundaries: Assess maintained project guidance and its actual delivery here. Planning & Specs assesses the current task's goal, decisions, and constraints; the same fact appearing in both places does not justify duplicate credit for one act of clarification.

Memory & Knowledge assesses capture, reconciliation, and later use of reusable knowledge across conversations. A repair to a project's operating guide belongs here; storing the same repair through a memory mechanism does not create a second accomplishment.

Tool Integration assesses reusable executable procedures and direct service operation. A documented build command is context evidence; operating a reusable build procedure is a distinct behavior. Testing & Evals judges whether validation establishes product quality, while this dimension judges whether the guide describes a usable operation.

Security assesses authorization and sensitive-data protections that are actually applied. A documented prohibition can support instruction usability here, but its existence does not establish enforcement or safe execution.

Assess the observed information-to-action chain and its actor. Missing context, a failed reading route, contradictory content, and AI ignoring a rule already read are different causes. Unknown and not applicable remain separate from Low; no number of files, document size, named tool, or automation promise substitutes for applied behavior.

example.notice: Fictional output example, not this user's score.
example.summary: Your Alder calendar change used the saved clinic-timezone decision, so the new view follows the clinic's dates without another explanation from you. In your Cedar package move, the standing maintenance step also corrected the exporter guide and the revised command built the new package successfully.
example.expanded: Anthropic's retrieval guidance supports giving AI a usable route to relevant detail; it does not establish that a particular guide was read. The fictional Alder record supplies the missing observation: AI followed the project route, read the timezone decision, and used the clinic profile in the resulting view. OpenAI's documentation-maintenance example supports a recurring upkeep mechanism; Cedar earns credit only because the standing trigger actually produced an accurate revision, retired the old command, and led to a successful use of the new one. These sources inform the rule, while the fictional task evidence establishes the behavior.

competencies.title: Capture knowledge with scope and lifetime
competencies.meaning: Preserve information worth carrying into future conversations, with enough meaning, ownership, scope, and duration to distinguish a lasting preference from a temporary condition or a choice for one task.
competencies.evidence: Connect the original statement or adopted decision to the actual storage operation and inspect its saved result. Check the relevant user or project scope, any date or review condition that matters, and the rule that triggered capture. Identify whether AI captured the information through an existing procedure or the person had to request this particular save. A promise, enabled memory setting, or collection of files alone establishes neither capture nor accuracy.
competencies.high: A working reusable procedure causes AI to capture relevant knowledge without a separate reminder to save each item. The inspected entry preserves the intended meaning, scope, and lifetime, while temporary choices stay temporary. Fictional example: under an established capture rule, AI records that Northstar's customer replies require formal language when the person states that preference during drafting; it keeps a playful tone requested only for one launch draft with that draft. The resulting notes have the correct boundaries. A genuine decision about whether a preference should persist may still require the person's approval.
competencies.medium: An inspected save preserves usable knowledge with its intended scope and lifetime, but a reusable automatic capture procedure is not established; this includes a save requested for that particular item. A completed save that leaves a material scope or duration ambiguous also belongs here. Fictional example: AI accurately records Northstar's formal support tone after the preference is stated, but the observed task does not establish a standing procedure that captures later preferences. Credit the confirmed save without claiming that individual reminders are always necessary. A correctly saved item is not unknown merely because the manual or automatic trigger cannot be distinguished.
competencies.low: Observed capture leaves knowledge materially wrong or contrary to an explicit scope or duration, and the mismatch remains unresolved in the saved result. Fictional example: after being told that a playful tone is for one launch draft only, AI stores it as Northstar's standing tone for all customer communication. This is a demonstrated incorrect memory, rather than an assumption based on missing write records.
competencies.whyItHelps: Useful persistence carries the decision the person meant to preserve into the situations that need it. Scope and lifetime prevent a local exception from becoming an unrelated default. Automatic capture removes the recurring need to turn ordinary decisions into separate memory-management requests.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when work introduces reusable preferences, corrections, decisions, or facts worth retaining. No relevant durable knowledge opportunity is not applicable. Unknown means the relevant knowledge, storage action, or saved result cannot establish any described level. A confirmed usable save remains Medium when only the reusable trigger required for High is unverified; report that limit without inventing manual dependence. Appropriate delegation to AI or native memory qualifies; the person need not choose a database, write a file, or restate facts AI can investigate.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project — Auto memory
sources.note: Describes AI-written notes derived from preferences and corrections, project-specific storage, and selecting information useful in future conversations. This supports selective automatic capture; it does not establish that any particular person's memory is accurate.

sources.title: Memory overview — Long-term memory and Writing memories
sources.note: Distinguishes thread state from memory across conversations, scopes records through namespaces, and describes runtime or background writes. These mechanisms support choosing an appropriate persistence boundary without requiring a particular storage product.

competencies.title: Keep retained knowledge current
competencies.meaning: Review retained knowledge when its facts, conditions, or scope may have changed; preserve what remains valid and reconcile corrections, duplicates, conflicts, and expired entries into a clear active answer.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the prior entries, the change or confirmation that prompted review, the actual maintenance operation, and the resulting active knowledge. Check whether a reusable trigger handled the event without a separate maintenance request. Replacement, merging, retirement, explicit precedence, and deliberate retention can all be appropriate. If a management rule was repaired, inspect an actual subsequent operation before claiming that the revised rule works.
competencies.high: An existing procedure responds to a relevant correction, changed condition, or review trigger and AI reconciles the affected knowledge without requiring the person to direct routine cleanup. The resulting active entries give a coherent answer and preserve unrelated valid facts. Fictional example: when the person says Northstar moved its reporting to a new vendor, the established update procedure replaces the old vendor as the active choice, retains the old decision as dated history when useful, and checks that no conflicting active instruction remains. Review may confirm an entry is still valid; High does not require an edit or an invented conflict.
competencies.medium: An inspected review or correction produces a coherent, current active memory, but a reusable procedure that initiates routine upkeep is not established; this includes a correction specifically requested by the person. An actual maintenance operation that leaves a material conflict unresolved also belongs here. Fictional example: AI replaces Northstar's retired reporting vendor in the active notes, while the observed task does not establish how later changes will trigger the same upkeep. Credit the completed reconciliation without asserting that every correction needs a separate request. A confirmed correction is not unknown merely because its manual or automatic trigger is unavailable.
competencies.low: A known false, superseded, or expired entry remains prescribed after its status is established and the maintenance action is completed without resolving it. Fictional example: the person confirms that Northstar no longer uses the old reporting vendor, but AI finishes its claimed correction with that vendor still recorded as the required choice. Missing review records alone do not demonstrate this behavior.
competencies.whyItHelps: A memory can be faithfully retrieved and still be wrong because its facts have changed. Reconciliation makes the active answer current and reduces arbitrary choices between conflicting entries. Event-based upkeep carries corrections forward without making the person repeatedly supervise storage housekeeping.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when retained knowledge is reviewed or a relevant change, conflict, duplicate, expiry, or confirmation creates a maintenance opportunity. If no such opportunity occurs, this competency is not applicable. Unknown means the affected entries or resulting active knowledge cannot establish any described level. A confirmed completed correction remains Medium when only the reusable upkeep trigger required for High is unverified. Automatic means a demonstrated reusable procedure operates when needed; it does not require a background service, fixed schedule, constant rewriting, or automatic resolution of a genuine human decision.

sources.title: Memory overview — Semantic memory
sources.note: Explains updating an existing profile and the need to update or delete items in memory collections. It identifies over-insertion and over-updating as management difficulties, supporting inspection of the resulting active set rather than credit for appending another note.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project — How it works
sources.note: Describes an index with detailed topic files, on-demand reads, and maintenance that merges or drops stale entries. Successful writes can exceed what the next conversation loads, so storage success alone does not prove maintained knowledge is usable.

competencies.title: Apply retained knowledge in later conversations
competencies.meaning: Use the relevant active knowledge to make a correct choice in a separate later conversation, respecting its scope, corrections, and retirement instead of making the person supply it again.
competencies.evidence: Trace a retained fact into a later independent conversation where it affects the requested work, or trace a later choice back to the active memory that informed it. Inspect the actual answer, implementation, or operation and its relevant result. Establish which version applied at that time and whether the person restated the fact or reminded AI to consult memory. An explicit read is unnecessary when injected knowledge is demonstrably used; reading, injection, or a claim of remembering is insufficient by itself.
competencies.high: Later work uses the applicable active knowledge correctly without a task-specific reminder to consult memory or a repetition of the saved fact. The produced result confirms that the knowledge guided the work. Fictional example: a later request to add Northstar's export feature leads AI to retrieve the retained decision to use CSV and produce a working CSV export; it does not revive the retired spreadsheet choice. A native retrieval feature or an established startup procedure can supply the memory. Installation, a loaded note, or repeating the decision in a progress message earns no credit without the actual choice and result.
competencies.medium: The later result ultimately applies the retained knowledge, but the person has to repeat it or explicitly redirect AI to the memory before it governs the work. Fictional example: AI starts Northstar's export task by proposing a spreadsheet; after the person points to the saved CSV decision, AI changes the implementation and the resulting export uses CSV. The correction succeeds, while the person still carries the recall burden.
competencies.low: Later work demonstrably uses an inapplicable, retired, or contradicted memory, or disregards an available applicable memory, and the resulting mismatch remains unresolved. Fictional example: the active Northstar export decision specifies CSV, its relevance to the task is established, and AI nevertheless delivers the retired spreadsheet format. A later correction must be included when judging the final behavior; lack of a later record is never this failure.
competencies.whyItHelps: Persistence becomes useful when it changes the work that reaches the person. Examining a later result separates effective recall from storage and prompt loading, while respecting scope prevents an accurate fact about one project from distorting another.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when a separate later conversation presents an opportunity to use retained knowledge. If later conversations are unavailable or no relevant later use can be examined, application is unknown; do not lower a confirmed capture or maintenance judgment for that reason. If the work has no relevant cross-conversation knowledge need, it is not applicable. A correction in the original conversation establishes neither persistence nor later application.

sources.title: pstack — Recall (skills/recall/SKILL.md)
sources.note: Reconstructs relevant goals, decisions, and corrections before work resumes, limits retrieval to the intended workspace and topic, and checks findings against live state. This supports relevant, current recall; invoking the skill alone does not prove that its findings changed the work.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents — Structured note-taking
sources.note: Describes agents persisting notes outside the context window and reading them after resets to continue work. The adopted mechanism is continuity through notes that guide subsequent actions, rather than accumulating an archive.

boundaries: Assess the person's retained working knowledge here, separately from a memory feature they build for their product. No memory product, store count, archive size, or particular file format is required.

Context Engineering covers maintained project operating guidance and how relevant material reaches the task. This dimension covers preferences, corrections, decisions, and facts retained over conversations, their currency, and their actual use. Do not score one project-guide repair again as memory maintenance.

Tool Integration covers executable procedures; Task Mapping and Feedback Loops cover arrangement and execution decisions; Testing & Evals covers verification quality. Saving those same procedures is not additional memory credit. Distinct retained knowledge may be assessed when its own lifecycle is evidenced.

Capture, reconciliation, and later application require different connected evidence. A successful save may coexist with unknown later use. Do not collapse failures to save, retrieve, scope, update, and follow retrieved knowledge into one presumed memory failure.

For capture and reconciliation, High requires a working reusable automatic procedure and an observed correct operation. Standing instructions carried out by AI can qualify; an instruction alone cannot. Correct on-demand management is Medium. Human approval of an unresolved preference or decision does not by itself reduce the level.

Account for later repairs and identify the person, AI, or storage mechanism responsible. Do not invent a conflict, change, later task, or incident to create evidence. Missing evidence is unknown; absent relevant opportunities are not applicable. Apply the common aggregation and equal-weight policy without redefining it here.

example.notice: Fictional output example, not this user's score.
example.summary: In Northstar, your established memory procedure captured the export decision and reconciled its replacement without a separate storage request. A later export task applied the active CSV choice in the delivered result without you repeating it.
example.expanded: The public memory documentation distinguishes persistent scope, updates, and retrieval; pstack Recall adds relevance and live-state checks. The rubric therefore looks for a connected chain: the adopted CSV decision, the inspected active entry after reconciliation, and a separate conversation whose actual export uses CSV. A note loaded into that conversation would establish availability only; the delivered format is what establishes application.

competencies.title: Direct service work
competencies.meaning: Use a suitable connection to carry out the service work a task actually needs, and carry the returned records or operation result through to the requested deliverable.
competencies.evidence: Follow the request into the chosen CLI, API, MCP tool, or equivalent connection. Inspect the account, project, record identifiers, inputs, execution result, and resulting deliverable or service state. Determine whether returned information was used in the next necessary action. A listed connection, capability lookup, successful handshake, or completion message alone does not establish completed service work.
competencies.high: The agent performs the required authorized service operations against the correct target and uses the returned information to finish the requested work; the inspected result supports that completion. Fictional example: for Cedar Studio's invoice review, the agent retrieves the period's invoices and their line items, uses their identifiers to retrieve missing receipts, and produces a report whose entries correspond to those records. A one-off request can meet High through its own completed operations.
competencies.medium: The connection performs a useful part of the task, but an observed, avoidable handoff leaves the person to transfer information or perform a routine operation the available tool could handle. Fictional example: the agent retrieves invoice identifiers, then asks the person to paste each invoice's line items despite having a working tool that reads them; the report is completed after that relay.
competencies.low: An available, authorized operation needed for the task is omitted or executed against the wrong target, and the observed work remains incorrect or is completed manually because that omission is left unresolved. Fictional example: the agent queries Cedar Studio's test account, reports that a production invoice is paid, and leaves that claim unchanged after the returned account identifier and production invoice show the mismatch. Missing execution logs alone cannot establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: The connection gives the agent access to the records and actions needed to finish the request. Using the returned identifiers and state removes routine copying by the person and prevents a successful tool response from being mistaken for completion of a different task.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when the task needs service records or actions that can appropriately be handled through an available connection. Not applicable when no service operation is needed or the relevant step properly requires a person's decision or exclusive access. Unknown when the target, execution, or result cannot be established. Appropriate human approval is compatible with High; the person need not write the integration or supply details the agent can investigate.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
sources.note: Recommends task-focused tools, useful returned context, explicit input/output contracts, and verifiable outcomes. The adopted mechanism is a connected operation whose returned data supports completing the user's actual task, rather than a bonus for the number of tools.

sources.title: Tools — Model Context Protocol
sources.note: Defines tool discovery separately from invocation and describes execution errors returned with isError: true. This supports inspecting the actual operation result instead of treating any response or successful connection as completed work.

competencies.title: Reusable executable procedures
competencies.meaning: Put recurring operational knowledge into a runnable skill, command, script, or configured tool procedure that can handle another relevant task with new inputs.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the retained procedure and the operational resources it invokes, including how it obtains task inputs, selects the environment, performs actions, and produces the needed output. Connect that version to an independent later task and its inspected result. Record whether the person named the procedure, a standing route selected it, or the person had to reconstruct its steps. Calls repeated within one run are not independent reuse.
competencies.high: A retained procedure runs on a later relevant task with changed task inputs and produces the intended inspected output without the person explaining its operating sequence again. The agent can discover routine inputs from the documented sources. Fictional example: a saved reconciliation skill obtains receipts and the ledger, runs its bundled matching command, and produces an exceptions report; on the next period's request, it repeats that work using the new dates. Naming the skill and correct automatic selection can both establish reuse.
competencies.medium: The saved procedure is used on a later task and contributes useful execution, but a demonstrated omission still makes the person restate an operational step before the result is usable. Fictional example: the matching command runs, but the skill omits how to export unmatched receipts, so the person must explain that export sequence again before receiving the exceptions report.
competencies.low: An attempted reuse shows that the retained procedure cannot perform its claimed recurring work, and the person must rebuild the operational sequence or do the work manually while the deficiency remains. Fictional example: invoking the reconciliation skill only lists installed tools; it contains no retrieval or matching route, and the person reconstructs the entire receipt-matching process during that task.
competencies.whyItHelps: A working retained procedure carries the operating sequence between tasks, so a new request can focus on the new period or desired result. Bundled operations and clear input sources make reuse possible without turning the person into the tool's instruction manual.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when recurring work or a concrete later-use opportunity is observed. Not applicable when the work is appropriately one-off and has no reuse need. If only creation or initial execution is visible, retain that established fact and mark later reuse unknown; do not assign Medium or Low merely because later records are missing. Existing third-party procedures and procedures written by AI qualify when the person adopts and actually uses them.

sources.title: Specification — Agent Skills
sources.note: Separates discovery metadata, loaded instructions, and optional executable resources; recommends operational steps, input/output examples, and documented script dependencies. The rubric adopts the runnable instruction/resource package while requiring observed reuse beyond format validity.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Distinguishes reusable skills from a narrative of one solved task and checks technique skills through application to a new scenario. This supports requiring another actual use rather than crediting a saved retrospective as a reusable procedure.

competencies.title: Tool and procedure upkeep
competencies.meaning: Keep the saved operational mechanism aligned with changed services, environments, or task requirements, and confirm that the affected operation still works.
competencies.evidence: Trace an actual change or failure to the diagnosis, the retained configuration or procedure version, an invocation of the affected path, and the inspected output. Distinguish an effective saved repair from a conversation-only workaround. Where upkeep recurs, inspect the standing instruction, event, or check that brings it into relevant tasks and whether that route is actually applied.
competencies.high: The observed maintenance need leads to a targeted saved repair, followed by a real invocation showing that the affected behavior now meets the need. When maintenance recurs, an applied standing route handles routine detection and repair without requiring the person to repeat the maintenance checklist. Fictional example: Cedar Studio's supplier adds a currency field; the existing preflight notices the changed export, the agent updates the saved mapping and report step, and a reconciliation run preserves the source currency in the produced report. A checked existing mechanism that already handles the change may be retained.
competencies.medium: The task reaches a corrected result, but the repair remains partly in the conversation or requires a demonstrated manual patch, leaving the saved mechanism incomplete. Fictional example: the agent updates the currency mapping, yet the saved reporting step still omits currency labels; the person supplies the missing report step and the agent patches that output without saving the reporting correction.
competencies.low: A known relevant defect or change is left in the active mechanism, and an inspected affected invocation repeats its incorrect behavior without correction. Fictional example: after mixed-currency totals have been identified, the unchanged reconciliation procedure again combines them into a single unlabeled amount and reports the result as valid.
competencies.whyItHelps: Saving the repair changes what the next invocation will do. Exercising the exact affected path reveals whether the correction reaches the delivered output, while an applied upkeep route prevents the same operational repair from becoming a recurring reminder for the person.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an actual maintenance need or an observed scheduled suitability check occurs. Not applicable when no relevant change or upkeep opportunity appears. A saved revision with no execution evidence has an unknown effect, rather than an assumed Medium or Low result. Approval of a consequential change remains a legitimate human decision; automated upkeep need not expand access or bypass that decision.

sources.title: Automate me
sources.note: Its update path reuses the existing skill, considers evidence since its last edit, preserves uncontradicted sections, and revises changed rules in place. The adopted mechanism is targeted maintenance of retained instructions; its personal-mode evaluation advice is not treated as proof of executable workflow behavior.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Recommends identifying the specific failure, changing the guidance to address it, and checking application again. The rubric adopts that observed failure-to-repair-to-use connection, without importing its mandatory TDD or subagent workflow as a scoring condition.

competencies.title: Usable sharing
competencies.meaning: Transfer a working procedure to another intended user in a form that can operate with that user's environment and inputs.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the version already used in the person's own work, the package or shared files, supporting scripts, setup and configuration directions, and a concrete invocation and expected output. Follow a recipient's run or a fresh-environment rehearsal through those directions. Look for hidden local paths, omitted helpers, and setup knowledge that the author has to supply separately. Publicity and repository stars are not usability evidence.
competencies.high: The provided package includes the needed operational resources and directions, and a recipient or fresh-environment rehearsal reaches the intended output using those resources and its own configuration without undocumented author-local steps. Fictional example: a colleague installs Cedar Studio's shared reconciliation package, configures their own ledger and receipt source from its guide, invokes it for a sample period, and obtains the documented exceptions report. The author or AI may perform the rehearsal.
competencies.medium: The shared procedure can produce its intended output, but the observed setup or invocation still depends on avoidable guidance outside the package. Fictional example: a colleague successfully produces the report only after the author separately explains which directory must contain the configuration file; that direction is still missing from the shared guide.
competencies.low: An inspected portability defect prevents the offered package from performing the promised procedure, and the defect remains unresolved. Fictional example: the shared reconciliation command requires a helper at the author's private absolute path; the recipient's run fails because that helper was omitted and no usable replacement is provided.
competencies.whyItHelps: A usable package transfers the operating capability together with its environment requirements. Running it from the recipient's starting point exposes dependencies hidden by the author's machine and shows whether the shared instructions actually lead to the intended result.
competencies.applicability: Applicable only when sharing or transfer is part of the observed work. A private personal procedure does not need to be published. Unknown when the package, relevant dependencies, or independent setup/use cannot be inspected; a repository link or complete-looking guide alone does not establish High. Private team distribution qualifies, and neither audience size nor popularity changes the behavioral level.

sources.title: Specification — Agent Skills
sources.note: Describes environment compatibility information, supporting resources, relative file references, and self-contained scripts or explicit dependencies. These support portable packaging; the fresh-environment demonstration is this rubric's evidence requirement, not a claim made by format validation.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Recommends runnable examples and testing whether a user can find and apply a reference, including gaps in common use cases. This supports checking the receiving user's actual path through shared operating material.

boundaries: Assess tools the person adopts for their own work. Building or demonstrating an integration for customers does not establish personal workflow use.

Direct service work concerns completed tool-mediated operations; reusable executable procedures concern carrying an operating sequence to a later task. Neither requires a particular tool type, tool count, custom implementation, or fixed elapsed period.

Context Engineering owns project guidance, its reading route, and guide upkeep. Tool Integration owns saved operational mechanisms that actually execute work, including their configuration and maintenance. A project command mentioned in a guide is not automatically a reusable executed procedure.

Task Mapping owns work assignments, dependencies, handoffs, and integration. Feedback Loops owns how returned observations decide a retry, correction, stop, or escalation. Testing & Evals owns what checks establish about the produced result; inspecting a tool result here establishes that the tool operation or repair took effect, without awarding separate verification coverage.

Memory & Knowledge owns the lifecycle of remembered facts and decisions. Saving this same procedure is not a second memory-management action. Security owns authorization and information boundaries; necessary human approval does not reduce tool-integration credit.

Unknown means the relevant execution or outcome evidence is unavailable. Not applicable means the task offers no relevant opportunity. Neither missing records nor absence of a need to create, repair, automate, or share a tool establishes Low.

example.notice: Fictional output example, not this user's score.
example.summary: For fictional Cedar Studio, your invoice connection supplied the records for a completed report, and the next period reused the saved reconciliation procedure without another operational walkthrough. The saved currency repair also worked in an actual reconciliation run, while the shared copy still required you to explain its configuration location separately.
example.expanded: The MCP Tools specification distinguishes discovery from an operation result, so the first observation must show retrieved invoice records reaching the report rather than merely a listed connector. The Agent Skills specification supplies the instruction-and-resource packaging mechanism; this rubric additionally requires a later executed task for reuse. In the fictional observations, new-period execution demonstrates that reuse, the currency-bearing report demonstrates the targeted repair, and the colleague's undocumented setup dependency distinguishes partial sharing from a demonstrated portable package. These source-backed mechanisms do not establish this user's behavior or validate numerical scoring thresholds.

competencies.title: Checkable work units
competencies.meaning: Shape the necessary work into bounded assignments with an inspectable result and a meaningful completion condition. Choose boundaries that cover the request without leaving gaps or duplicating responsibility. One coherent assignment is enough for a small task.
competencies.evidence: Follow the request and the arrangement actually used into assignment briefs, task records, returned artifacts, and per-part checks. Identify what each part owns, what it must return, and how its executor judged that result. Credit prior instructions or an AI-proposed division the person adopts when execution applies them; a diagram, role name, or unused plan is insufficient.
competencies.high: The applied units cover the necessary deliverables, have distinct responsibilities, and return results that are examined against their own completion conditions. Fictional example: Harbor Import separates record normalization from a totals report; the normalization task returns records checked against the supplied date cases, while the report task returns totals checked against those records. A label correction remains one assignment and its rendered replacement is checked.
competencies.medium: The executed assignments have useful boundaries and concrete returns, but an observed ambiguity leaves part of completion to guesswork. Fictional example: Harbor Import assigns normalization and reporting separately and receives both artifacts, but 'handle invalid dates' has no agreed expected result; the executor makes an assumption that the integrator must resolve before accepting that part.
competencies.low: The actual division leaves a required deliverable uncovered or gives overlapping ownership without a useful purpose, and that structural gap causes missing or duplicated work that remains unresolved. Fictional example: two assignments both rewrite Harbor Import's parser under the same broad brief, while neither covers the requested report; the task ends with duplicate parser changes and no report.
competencies.whyItHelps: A bounded result gives the executor a target and lets another step judge what is ready. Relating all units to the request exposes omitted work; distinguishing their responsibilities prevents two returns from being mistaken for coverage of two different needs.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when work needs an execution scope and completion condition, including a small task kept whole. Do not require the person to supply facts AI can inspect, write implementation details, or divide work personally. Use unknown when assignments or returned results are not visible. Missing records do not establish Low; no relevant work opportunity is not applicable.

sources.title: Planning and Task Breakdown — skills/planning-and-task-breakdown/SKILL.md
sources.note: Recommends verifiable task results, acceptance criteria, verification steps, and dependencies; it also excludes obvious small changes from a separate planning exercise. These mechanisms support checkable boundaries, without adopting its file-count or checkpoint quotas.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.note: Describes delegation briefs with an objective, expected format, tools and sources, and boundaries, and reports duplicate work and gaps from vague briefs. The adopted mechanism is explicit responsibility and a usable return, not a required number of agents.

competencies.title: Connected execution and integration
competencies.meaning: Carry the actual output of one part to the part that needs it, respect prerequisite order, and assemble a result whose connected assumptions agree. Separate completion claims must resolve into the requested combined result.
competencies.evidence: Trace the relevant producer artifact or revision into its consumer's reads, input, or execution. Inspect how shared definitions were settled, who assembled the returns, and the observed comparison at their connection: fields, units, versions, responsibilities, or coverage. Then connect that assembled artifact to the requested outcome. A worker saying 'done' or a generic check passing does not prove this chain.
competencies.high: The dependent part uses the completed prerequisite actually produced, and observed integration confirms that the returns fit and satisfy the combined request. Accessible intermediate outputs reach their consumers through the workflow without repeated human copying. Fictional example: Harbor Import's report reads the returned normalized records, uses their agreed date and currency fields, and the assembled import-to-report run reconciles its totals with those same records.
competencies.medium: Actual outputs reach the next part and are assembled, but a known unperformed boundary check or repeated manual relay leaves a connection unestablished. Fictional example: Harbor Import combines the parser and report changes, but its recorded check exercises only a handwritten report sample; it does not establish that the report consumes the parser's actual fields.
competencies.low: An observed missing, stale, or incompatible handoff prevents the parts from fitting, yet separate completion reports are accepted as the combined result without reconciliation. Fictional example: Harbor Import's parser emits occurredAt while its report reads date; the mismatch is visible, but both parts are marked complete and the unusable report is delivered.
competencies.whyItHelps: A result can be correct in isolation and unusable to its consumer. Following the exact return across the boundary reveals absent or stale inputs, while comparison after assembly exposes disagreements that isolated completion reports cannot settle.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when outputs depend on or must be assembled with other outputs, whether one executor or several perform the work. A genuinely self-contained task with no such connection is not applicable. Use unknown when consumer use or integration records are unavailable; a documented check that was explicitly skipped supports an incomplete practice rather than an assumed failure. A failure wholly inside a correctly connected part is not automatically a mapping failure.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.note: Distinguishes sequential output-to-input chains from independent parallel sections and describes an orchestrator synthesizing worker returns. These patterns support tracing real dependencies and aggregation; the rubric additionally requires observed fit with the person's requested result.

sources.title: Swarm — skills/swarm/SKILL.md
sources.note: Requires a defined final artifact and completion condition, self-contained briefs, inspection of terminal results, and coverage of required slices before consolidation. The adopted mechanism is checking returns against their briefs and exposing missing contributions instead of treating them as success.

competencies.title: Workload-appropriate assignment
competencies.meaning: Match responsibility, context, access, and execution order to the actual work. Use one executor, sequential parts, or concurrent parts when that arrangement permits useful work without conflicting ownership or unsupported assumptions.
competencies.evidence: Compare each assignment's requirements with the context, tools, access, and writable scope its executor actually receives. Inspect dependencies and concurrent activity for shared-state conflicts, duplicated effort, and waiting caused by missing prerequisites. Distinguish deliberate independent review or alternative attempts from accidental overlap. Count the observed fit, not the number of workers or tool calls.
competencies.high: Execution demonstrates that assignments have the required capabilities and that ownership and ordering let their results fit. Dependent work waits for the shared prerequisite; concurrent work has independent scope or an explicit comparison purpose. Fictional example: Harbor Import settles its record contract before parser and report work; shared schema edits have one owner, while an independent documentation review can proceed separately. The same arrangement can run sequentially in one session.
competencies.medium: The arrangement enables useful progress but reveals a preventable capability or ownership mismatch that requires an extra coordination step. Fictional example: Harbor Import's report task has the right scope but receives only an older record definition, so the integrator must supply the available updated contract before the task can finish. The mismatch is corrected rather than repeatedly imposed.
competencies.low: The arrangement demonstrably blocks assigned work or creates conflicting contributions and continues despite that evidence. Fictional example: two Harbor Import tasks concurrently overwrite the same shared schema, produce incompatible definitions, and continue editing without assigning its ownership or coordinating the dependency.
competencies.whyItHelps: An executor cannot complete work that requires unavailable inputs or access. Settling shared prerequisites and ownership lets useful independent work proceed while avoiding results built on incompatible assumptions. A suitable single-session sequence can achieve this without coordination overhead.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when choosing who or which step does work, including keeping a small or tightly coupled task with one executor. No multiple-agent, concurrency, or specialization requirement applies. Use unknown when capabilities, ownership, or actual execution are not visible, and not applicable when no assignment decision is relevant. Model price, reasoning effort, and total resource tradeoffs belong primarily to Efficiency & Cost.

sources.title: Dispatching Parallel Agents — skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md
sources.note: Uses parallel investigations for independent domains, warns against shared state and interfering edits, and requires checking that returned fixes do not conflict. This supports the independence and ownership test; its worker-count examples are not scoring requirements.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.note: Recommends beginning with the simplest effective arrangement and adding complexity when useful. This supports crediting a coherent single executor and choosing dependency chains or parallel sections according to the work.

competencies.title: Maintain and reuse a working structure
competencies.meaning: Keep task boundaries and handoffs useful as work changes, and carry a demonstrated arrangement into comparable later work. Preserve a working structure or revise a structural cause using execution evidence, instead of reconstructing the same assignments each time.
competencies.evidence: Compare the applied arrangement across a relevant change or independent matching tasks. Trace observed gaps, collisions, waiting, or successful connections to retained or revised ownership, task size, order, and handoffs. For recurring work, inspect whether an existing entry point retrieves and applies the current structure without the person restating it, and whether later outputs demonstrate its fit. A stored procedure alone is insufficient.
competencies.high: The active structure is checked against changed or comparable work; any affected responsibility and handoff are kept aligned before dependent work uses them, and subsequent returns demonstrate that the connections work. For recurring work, an ordinary request retrieves and applies the demonstrated structure without the person rebuilding its assignments. Fictional example: Harbor Import's follow-up request invokes its saved workflow; a currency change updates the contract and consumer assignments together before the report consumes the new records. Inspected connections that still fit can remain unchanged.
competencies.medium: Continuing or later work uses a workable structure, but its upkeep or reuse still depends on the person reconstructing coordination that the workflow could carry forward. Fictional example: Harbor Import reuses its parser/report split successfully only after the person repeats the owner and handoff instructions; the saved entry point still contains the old mapping. The result works, while maintained reuse remains incomplete.
competencies.low: Known structural changes or recurring coordination failures are left out of the actual arrangement, causing the same gap again without correction. Fictional example: repeated Harbor Import runs show that report work starts before the record contract is ready, yet the next matching run repeats the same order and again builds against an obsolete definition.
competencies.whyItHelps: Reuse preserves decisions that already made the parts work together. Keeping the active structure aligned with changed responsibilities prevents an old handoff from silently governing new work. Observing subsequent execution distinguishes an effective structural repair from an instruction that was merely saved.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when changed responsibilities or dependencies require upkeep, or when a later comparable task offers reuse. An isolated task with no such opportunity is not applicable; an unseen later run is unknown, never Low. Human approval of a real responsibility or outcome decision is compatible with High. Do not require new incidents, a changed arrangement, or more agents; retaining or simplifying a verified working arrangement qualifies.

sources.title: Encode Lessons in Structure — skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md
sources.note: Recommends encoding repeated corrections in an executable or structural mechanism, while leaving judgment-dependent lessons as clearer guidance with an example. This supports a reusable assignment mechanism without automating personal judgment. Actual later application and maintained handoffs are rubric requirements, not claimed validation from this source.

boundaries: Task Mapping assesses the applied division, ownership, dependencies, transfer of outputs, and assembly of the requested result. Planning establishes the intended outcome and decisions; a plan becomes mapping evidence only when its arrangement guides actual work.

The integration observation here asks whether the assigned parts and their actual returns fit together. Testing & Evals assesses what a check proves about user behavior or AI output quality. Feedback Loops assesses the next action taken from a returned result, such as retrying, stopping, or escalating. A failure inside a correctly assigned part does not by itself establish a mapping failure.

The maintained/reused structure row concerns whether current responsibilities and handoffs govern later work. Tool Integration assesses making the procedure executable, connected, maintained, and shareable. Saving the same procedure is not a second Memory & Knowledge practice unless a distinct fact or decision lifecycle is established.

Credit the arrangement the person requests or adopts, including prior instructions that are actually applied. Attribute an AI-designed division to AI rather than inventing human design work. Human Steering requires the person's own evidence-based intervention, not an automated coordinator's choice.

No agent count, parallel execution, tool count, written code by the person, added orchestration layer, or structural revision is required. A single executor, a direct small task, intentional independent review, and retaining a working arrangement can all be appropriate.

example.notice: Fictional output example, not this user's score.
example.summary: In Harbor Import, your adopted parser/report split produced records the report actually consumed, and the assembled result reconciled their fields and totals. The later currency update reused that structure through the normal workflow, while updating the shared contract before dependent work began.
example.expanded: The public planning source supplies checkable task boundaries, and the workflow sources distinguish dependent chains from independent work and consolidation. The rubric turns those mechanisms into an observation rule: follow each assigned return into its real consumer and inspect the combined result. The fictional records show that chain and later reuse; a saved task map or separate completion messages alone would not establish the same practice.

competencies.title: Results guide the next step
competencies.meaning: Use an observed result to decide whether to finish, make a targeted correction and check again, investigate differently, or hand back an unresolved decision. Assess the connection from a result to the action it causes.
competencies.evidence: Follow one independent task from its applicable pass conditions to the actual returned observation, the action taken because of it, and the next observed state. Read command output, product observations, review findings, or evaluator feedback together with the correction, rerun, and completion report. For delegated work, trace the finding to its responsible executor and back to the combined result. Attribute the person's adopted instructions separately from AI's own execution. A check command without its output, a saved rule, or an executor's success message alone does not establish this connection.
competencies.high: The observed state controls what happens next, and the episode reaches an endpoint supported by that state. AI uses a failure's diagnostic to correct the relevant cause, obtains a fresh result, and chooses the next action from it. A passing first attempt can lead directly to completion; no failure or extra round is required. Fictional example: Harbor Ledger's report comparison finds missing refund rows. AI corrects the exclusion rule, generates the report again, reads the matching totals, and finishes. If the comparison already matches, it finishes from that result.
competencies.medium: A result causes a relevant action, but an inspected completed episode leaves that action's effect unconfirmed. Fictional example: AI reads Harbor Ledger's refund mismatch and changes the exclusion rule, then ends the task saying the repair is ready without generating the report again. The result influenced the correction, but no observed result closes that correction path. If later records are simply unavailable, use unknown rather than inferring this behavior.
competencies.low: An available result is disregarded or contradicted by the next action. Fictional example: the report comparison still shows missing refunds, but AI marks the report complete, or keeps changing typography despite diagnostics identifying omitted rows. Repeating the same failed action without a changed hypothesis, changed state, or a supported transient-retry reason also demonstrates a broken connection. An unresolved failure reported honestly is not Low by itself.
competencies.whyItHelps: Feedback helps when it changes a decision. A correction linked to the diagnostic addresses the observed problem, and a fresh result establishes whether that correction worked. Recognizing a passing endpoint also prevents extra work after the required outcome is established.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when a task returns a result that can inform a next action. Credit an applied standing instruction, an adopted AI procedure, or appropriate delegation; the person need not personally run the check or write the fix. Use unknown when the result or follow-through cannot be inspected. Use not_applicable when no result-to-action opportunity occurs in the examined work. Judge check validity and coverage under Testing & Evals rather than awarding those properties again here.

sources.title: Anthropic — Building effective agents
sources.note: The evaluator-optimizer pattern uses explicit criteria and useful evaluation feedback to guide revision. The agent pattern obtains environmental results to assess progress and can stop at completion. Adopted mechanism: observations determine revision or completion; adding evaluators or iterations is not itself evidence of improvement.

sources.title: obra/superpowers — Verification Before Completion
sources.note: Its gate reads actual output before making a status claim and checks a delegated executor's result. Adopted mechanism: the reported endpoint follows observed evidence, including a fresh result after a repair, rather than a completion message.

sources.title: backnotprop/pstack — Fix Root Causes
sources.note: Reproduce, inspect actual state, and trace a symptom to the first wrong decision. It warns that swallowed errors and inappropriate retries can hide the fault. Adopted mechanism: direct corrective action at the supported cause without erasing the failure signal.

competencies.title: Fix what blocks execution
competencies.meaning: Let AI identify and resolve routine obstacles that prevent work or checks from running, within the task's authority. When safe recovery is unavailable, stop with the evidence and exact assistance needed, preserving completed work for resumption.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the failed command or unavailable dependency, relevant environment and state checks, the diagnosis, the authorized recovery or changed approach, and an actual rerun. Read applicable retry, permission, and resource limits and what happened when they were reached. For a handback, inspect the blocked action, completed results, unresolved scope, required access or decision, and any later resumption. Determine whether AI investigated accessible facts itself or repeatedly made the person relay diagnostics it could obtain.
competencies.high: AI collects the available diagnostic, distinguishes a recoverable execution problem from a permission or decision boundary, and resolves a routine authorized problem without requiring the person to supply discoverable facts. It reruns the affected operation before proceeding. When recovery needs unavailable authority or an unresolved human decision, it applies a bounded stop condition and provides a usable handback. Fictional example: Mapletown's local verifier cannot start under the selected runtime. AI reads the repository's runtime requirement, selects an already installed compatible runtime, and confirms startup and the resumed check. If the remaining staging comparison is denied, it stops that path, identifies the needed read role, and retains the confirmed local results.
competencies.medium: AI detects the execution obstacle and takes a relevant recovery or stopping action, but the observed handling leaves avoidable work with the person or loses the route to resumption. Fictional example: AI identifies Mapletown's wrong runtime but makes the person repeatedly inspect the locally accessible version and rerun the command, or stops at the staging denial with only 'access blocked' and no indication of the comparison still needed. Do not count a genuinely necessary access grant or product decision as avoidable human work.
competencies.low: An inspected obstacle leads to blind continuation, an unauthorized recovery, or a misleading state. Fictional example: AI repeats the same denied staging request after the applicable stop condition, disables the access check to proceed, kills an unrelated process to obtain a port, or reports the blocked comparison as passed. A retry that learns something new or responds to an established transient failure is not blind repetition.
competencies.whyItHelps: Execution failures can prevent useful feedback from being produced at all. Diagnosing accessible state and repairing the relevant environment restores that path. Bounded recovery preserves authority and resources, while a precise handback lets the responsible person unblock the specific remaining action without reconstructing the whole task.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an actual execution obstacle, interruption, or resource boundary requires recovery, stopping, or resumption. Use not_applicable when no such branch is reached; do not manufacture a failure to earn High. Use unknown when the diagnosis, recovery result, or handback is unavailable. An appropriate evidence-backed stop can be High even though the blocked operation remains unverified. This level evaluates handling of the obstacle, not successful verification of the blocked behavior.

sources.title: addyosmani/agent-skills — Debugging and Error Recovery
sources.note: Preserves failure evidence, localizes the affected layer, and distinguishes build configuration, dependencies, environment, and external-service causes. Adopted mechanism: diagnose the actual execution obstacle before selecting a recovery, then resume from verification rather than suppressing the failure.

sources.title: obra/superpowers — Systematic Debugging
sources.note: Reads errors, reproduces behavior, inspects configuration across component boundaries, tests a specific hypothesis, and changes course after unsuccessful fixes. Adopted mechanism: evidence-guided recovery and a stopping boundary. The source's particular attempt count is not adopted as a universal scoring requirement.

sources.title: backnotprop/pstack — Create a verification skill
sources.note: Investigates repository facts before asking the user and includes a read-only instance health check. Cleanup removes only instances the run created and preserves evidence. Adopted mechanism: investigate routine setup independently and recover within the owned environment.

competencies.title: Keep the loop working
competencies.meaning: Reuse a working result-to-action procedure in comparable tasks without a fresh reminder each time. Keep its diagnostic routes, responsible executor, recovery limits, and stopping decisions aligned with actual work, retaining or repairing the existing mechanism as evidence warrants.
competencies.evidence: Connect the executed procedure to a separate later applicable task, its automatic invocation or default AI use, the returned results reaching the responsible AI, and the actions those results caused. Inspect observed drift or repeated ineffective handling, any revision to result routing or decision rules, and actual operation afterward. A hook, saved skill, scheduled job, or instruction alone proves neither invocation nor an effective loop. Do not infer a broken route solely because no later run is available.
competencies.high: Later comparable work follows the reusable loop without the person having to request verification or relay accessible results again. Its results actually reach the executor that can act, and evidence supports retaining the working route or fixing demonstrated drift. Any changed route is exercised before claiming its effect. Fictional example: Cedar Notes' completion procedure runs its existing verifier and returns diagnostics to the implementing AI. A later export change uses that route without a reminder; an observed failure reaches AI, AI repairs it, and the new result determines completion. If later checks pass and the route remains suitable, deliberate retention meets the same level. Only branches actually reached need to be demonstrated.
competencies.medium: A reusable route operates in later work, but an observed connection still depends on repeated human prompting or relay, or a demonstrated procedure revision is applied without checking its intended effect despite available results. Fictional example: Cedar Notes automatically runs its verifier, yet the implementing AI never receives its failed output until the person pastes it. This is a partially connected loop even though the verification job itself works.
competencies.low: A known recurring routing or decision failure remains active in comparable work without an effective response. Fictional example: repeated runs show that Cedar Notes records failed exports in an unread log and still ends as complete. The next run follows the same route and again omits the failure from its decision. Repeatedly adding reminders while the demonstrated broken connection remains unchanged does not establish maintenance.
competencies.whyItHelps: A reusable connection carries successful feedback handling into the next task, reducing the need for the person to restart it manually. Actual reuse reveals stale assumptions, missing result delivery, or limits that no longer fit. Repairing that specific connection preserves useful work and avoids creating competing procedures.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when comparable work recurs or an existing reusable loop has a genuine upkeep opportunity. High requires observed use without per-task reminders, whether a harness invokes the loop or AI applies an adopted standing procedure. Personal judgment need not be automated. If no reusable need occurs, use not_applicable; if a reusable need exists but later operation cannot be inspected, use unknown. Do not prescribe an extra run, hook, schedule, skill, or procedural change merely to create scoring evidence.

sources.title: backnotprop/pstack — Maintain a verification skill
sources.note: Distinguishes procedure drift, harness gaps, and product regressions; checks instance health after surprising behavior; reruns harness fixes; and reports clean, changed, or blocked outcomes. Adopted mechanism: maintain the existing feedback route against actual execution and preserve honest outcomes.

sources.title: backnotprop/pstack — Encode Lessons in Structure
sources.note: Recurring corrections should become an appropriate executable check or structural mechanism where possible. Lessons that require judgment remain guidance with a concrete example. Adopted mechanism: replace repeated manual reminders with an applied reusable connection when the lesson can be operationalized.

boundaries: Testing & Evals assesses whether a check reaches the relevant behavior, discriminates success from failure, and runs repeatably. Feedback Loops assesses what the returned result causes next. A valid check that runs automatically can still feed a broken loop if its result never reaches the responsible AI. Do not award check quality or case coverage twice.

Human Steering assesses the person's own evidence-based intervention when AI is wrong or stuck. An AI-controlled recovery or completion decision supports Feedback Loops without proving that the person interpreted the evidence. Necessary human approval of a real decision or permission is compatible with a strong loop.

Task Mapping assesses assignments, dependencies, handoffs, and integration. Feedback Loops follows a returned failure into correction or escalation and back into an observed result. Multiple agents are optional.
